items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: So he was kind of my idol. When I grew up I wanted to put on a uniform and march in a parade. And you know he was always encouraging me to play music.

ctx.x: The grandfather you mentioned, was he the one that played with John Phillip Sousa?

Yes. How that came about was he was not a — my grandfather was born in Italy and he was a musician first. And then when he got married and came to the United States he had to support a family so he became a tailor. And he played gigs on the side. And a few times he was called to play with the Sousa band. And Sousa wanted him to, you know, be part of the — he was a great tuba player. And my grandmother said no dice, you know, you’d better stay home and make a living. So he wound up actually still being a great…
Now the tunes that you were hearing from the radio — jazz was really the popular music of the day —
